race_context: Clark-Pleasant Community School Corporation, headquartered in Whiteland in Johnson County, serves Whiteland, New Whiteland, parts of Greenwood and a very small section of Franklin, with Whiteland Community High School, Clark-Pleasant Middle School and five elementary schools {wiki_cp}. Whiteland Community High School reported 2,082 students in 2023-24; a current district-wide enrollment figure was not found in fetched sources {wiki_whs}.
Wikipedia lists Timothy Edsell as superintendent {wiki_whs}; his current contract status was not confirmed in fetched sources.
The board has five members: two represent Clark Township, two represent Pleasant Township and one is elected at large, according to IndyStar's 2022 filing roundup {indystar_2022}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows two Clark Township candidates (Kent Lewis Beeson and Linda Polesel) under 'vote for 1' and one Pleasant Township candidate (Kimberly Crawford) {in_list}{jc_list}. In 2022, three seats were on the ballot and Beeson and Polesel both ran in Clark Township, with Beeson and Crawford listed as incumbents {indystar_2022}. If the 2022 Clark Township contest filled both township seats for four-year terms, the 2026 Clark Township race would also elect two members, and both candidates would win; the true seat count was not confirmed in fetched sources and should be checked with the Johnson County election office.
Filing: Polesel filed May 28, 2026 and listed a Republican affiliation; Crawford filed June 9, 2026 as an Independent; Beeson filed June 18, 2026 with no party listed {jc_list}{inc_list}.

Operating referendum renewal: Clark-Pleasant asks voters Nov. 3, 2026 to continue its operating referendum levy for up to eight years at a rate of no more than $0.09 per $100 of assessed value, raising up to $4.4 million a year, to fund 'school safety initiatives, including the Clark-Pleasant police department, student support services and programming in response to reductions in property tax revenue' {dlgf_cp}. The ballot question says that if it is not approved, the tax bill on a $300,000 median residence would fall by $127 a year, and that the 2018 referendum it renews carried a $0.10 rate {dlgf_cp}. The state Department of Local Government Finance received the board's resolution and approved the ballot language on June 18, 2026 {dlgf_cp}.

Chalkbeat Indiana and WFYI's 2026 referendum guide lists Clark-Pleasant's $0.09 request among 38 Indiana district referendums and reports that many districts tie their requests to 2025's Senate Enrolled Act 1 property tax changes {chalkbeat_ref}.

Forums: no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or VOTE411 responses for these races were found in fetched sources. All three races appear uncontested in practice if the Clark Township race elects two members.
